title: Commanders Bye Week: We Can't Even Suck Good
seoTitle: Commanders Bye Week: Trade Deadline Takes, Group Chat Grief and Bingo
summary: The Commanders' bye week: a UVA trick-play heartbreak, Monday night as told by the group chat, a very official trade desk, why I'm a buyer anyway, and Bye Week Bingo.

bye-week-bingo.alt: A burgundy and gold bingo card titled Commanders Edition Bye Week Bingo, good through the Nov. 10 trade deadline. Squares include "Checked the Giants score anyway," "Someone brings up 1991," "We can't even suck good" and "Said next year in October." The free space reads "Still two games out."

paragraphs: No game this week. Just me, a 1-4-1 football team, two games of daylight between us and first place in the NFC East, and a trade deadline coming at us fast. The deadline is Tuesday, Nov. 10, at 4 p.m. Eastern. Before then we get the Eagles on Sunday night, Nov. 1, and the Rams on Nov. 8. Two days after the deadline, it's a Thursday night game at the Giants. Two games, a deadline and a short week, all in 12 days. It's a bye week, sure. It's also the calm before a very weird storm.
## The Undercard

Friday night, UVA hosted Duke, and I was up in the President's Box, where the food was on point and the vibe was immaculate. Then, with 1:14 left and Virginia up 16-13, Duke handed the ball to their running back, Nate Sheppard, who threw it 28 yards to a wide-open Brody Keefe for the winning touchdown. A running back. Threw it. To a man nobody was within a zip code of. Our last heave got picked off, because of course it did. Duke 19, Virginia 16.

I would like to file a formal complaint with whoever approves trick plays, and I would like it noted that I ate very well while filing it. UVA is 4-4. The Commanders are 1-4-1. My weekends have never been more balanced.
## Monday Night, As Told by the Group Chat
I didn't take great notes on Monday night, because I was on my couch on my birthday doing the thing I do, which is suffer. Luckily, the group chat took notes for me.

Here is Jason, in order. 10:45: "This won't happen, will it?" 10:53: "Holy shit this game has flipped." 10:56: "I will not believe, I will not believe, I will not believe." 10:57, the exact same sentence again, because once wasn't enough. 11:02: "Can't blow that timeout god dammit." 11:06: "Fuck I'm stressed." And at 11:10, simply: "I am sad." That's the entire Commanders experience in seven messages. You could frame it.
Chris, meanwhile, had a theory: "Refs heard from fans. They're trying to keep us in it." Then the last play happened, and Chris filed the official report: "They rush 3 and sack us."
My own contribution, for the record: "My butthole was semi puckered but man it was weirdly a game." I stand by every word.
## The Morning After

Tuesday morning was the debrief. Jason went first: "Other than Jayden I just am not seeing enough progress on this team. I'm struggling to figure out where we're any better than we were two years ago." Chris, more concisely: "We can't even suck good." That's the headline. That's the season so far. Thank you, Chris.

My theory, typed at 9:41 the next morning by a man who fell asleep on the couch and went upstairs around 12:30: "We have these AWESOME fucking years, like the RG3/Alfred Morris year, then trash. We have 2024, then trash. Like either be good or don't."

Chris thinks both coordinators are "too fresh," and that "we have so much stink on us keeping anything the same should be a deal breaker." Jason had been all about Blough taking over if Quinn ever got canned, and then added, "but man he is not giving me a ton of confidence right now." And the center situation came up, as it does. This offseason Washington cut its starting center, Tyler Biadasz, and as Jason put it, "It wasn't like we had huge savings from it either." His verdict: "The center thing was stupid from the second they did it, everyone knew it." Chris went further and called it "the biggest reason to fire AP." The group chat does not do trade deadlines quietly.
## The Trade Desk: Totally Real Offers
Adam Peters says teams are calling. In the spirit of transparency, here are the offers The Burgundy Wire is prepared to accept.
WASHINGTON ACQUIRES: one (1) professional lip reader, to translate our sideline for the rest of the country. SENDS: a conditional seventh-round pick. Condition: he never tells anyone what he saw.

WASHINGTON SIGNS: Scary Terry, the inflatable tube man out front of Högwaller, to the practice squad. With Terry McLaurin out for the season, we need a Terry. Route tree: up. Hands: debatable. Effort: relentless. He has never once stopped moving, which already puts him ahead of our offensive line.
WASHINGTON ACQUIRES: a timeout. Any timeout. Lightly used is fine. Jason, Monday night: "Can't blow that timeout god dammit." We would like a spare.
BEN SENDS: one (1) football, as promised on his birthday list, for the spike. RECEIVES: a win. STATUS: pending.
THE GROUP CHAT SENDS: Jason's 2-0-1 prediction record to the Giants. RECEIVES: future considerations.
## My Real Takes

Right now, I'm a buyer, and I can explain. Being a Commanders fan builds character, as I've always said, and character is mostly the ability to look at a 1-4-1 record and see a path. The NFC East is wide open. We're two games out of first. We're getting healthier, and Jayden is just being Jayden. JP Finlay pointed out that on Monday he became the first Washington quarterback to throw for 300 yards since Case Keenum in 2019. There's no reason not to believe we could randomly make a run and win a shitty NFC East. I've seen weirder. I've seen weirder from us.

Daron Payne is the hard one. He's been a stalwart on the defensive line since Washington drafted him in 2018, and his contract is up after this season. Paying him is going to be hard. But he's homegrown talent, and do we really just let him go? I don't know. I genuinely don't. If you know, write in.

Receiver is the obvious need, with Terry done for the year. Treylon Burks is a keeper, a #3 maybe, but we have something with him. Antonio Williams has kind of disappeared, and I think that's a scheme issue more than a him issue. So yes, get Jayden some weapons, which is also a square on the bingo card, which I am counting.
And if the NFC East weren't so bad, I would be all the way on the tank wagon for Jeremiah Smith, the Ohio State receiver, who is so nasty. But the NFC East is that bad. So: buyer.
One more for the plus column. Jason, Tuesday morning: "Sonny Styles too is awesome." He's right. Sonny is finally a nice pick.
## Bye Week Bingo

And because we have to do something with ourselves until Nov. 1, I made a bingo card. It's good through the trade deadline. Screenshot it, mark it up, and post your bingo. I'd like to report that "Checked the Giants score anyway" took no effort at all.

## Eagles Week Is Coming

Next up: the Eagles, Sunday, Nov. 1, 8:20 p.m., on national TV. Chris pointed out this week that I always have people whose faces I hate, and that they're "normally Dallas or Eagles coaches/players." He's not wrong. The list is long, and it is mostly Philadelphia.
Two games out, getting healthier, and a quarterback who keeps showing up even when the scoreboard doesn't. Being a Commanders fan builds character. This season is a lot of character. Hail.
